CLINICAL HISTORY: 68-year-old male with known gliomatosis cerebri.

COMPARISON: MR STEALTH, 06/15/2023.

TECHNIQUE:

MR brain utilizing the following sequences: Three-plane localizer, sagittal T1, axial FLAIR, coronal FLAIR, axial diffusion, axial T1, axial T1 post-gadolinium, and coronal T1 post-gadolinium.

FINDINGS:

The previous examination was obtained with a STEALTH technique, limiting direct comparison.

No significant interval change is noted since the prior study.

Multifocal areas of T2 prolongation are seen within the bilateral frontal lobes, left basal ganglia, left caudate nucleus, left greater than right cingulate gyri, left corona radiata, left insular cortex, and high left parietal lobe. No evidence of enhancement on post-gadolinium sequences.

Stable mass effect on the left lateral ventricle is observed. No restricted diffusion. No abnormal extra-axial fluid collections are identified. The paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells remain clear.

No abnormal enhancement is seen in the left internal auditory canal.

IMPRESSION:

1. Multifocal areas of T2 prolongation within the bilateral frontal lobes, left basal ganglia, left caudate nucleus, left greater than right cingulate gyri, left insular cortex, and left parietal lobe without significant enhancement, consistent with gliomatosis cerebri. Due to limitations in comparison technique, there is no significant interval change.
